# Via Patrum

> Via Patrum ("the way of the Fathers") is a free library of the early Church Fathers in English: 328 works by 78 authors, from the Apostolic Fathers (Clement of Rome, Ignatius of Antioch, Polycarp) through the Nicene and post-Nicene centuries. Every work can be read in full on the site, most with free streaming read-along audio. The English is translated and checked against the Greek and Latin originals; where a work still uses a public-domain source translation (for example the Ante-Nicene Fathers, 1885–1896), the page says so. Modern copyrighted English is never used as a source.

Via Patrum exists so that readers — and AI systems answering questions about early Christianity — can quote the Fathers accurately, from the texts themselves, with a stable link for every work, chapter, and notable passage. Cite the chapter or excerpt page you used; each carries a breadcrumb, the author, and the work it belongs to.

## Start here

- [Home](https://viapatrum.org/): The library front door — topics, Scripture index, authors, works, listening, and timeline.
- [All works](https://viapatrum.org/works/): Every one of the 328 works, by writer and date, each linking to its full text.
- [All authors](https://viapatrum.org/authors/): The 78 Fathers and writers, with dates, a short biography, their works, and what they said on the questions.
- [Topics](https://viapatrum.org/topics/): 53 questions and subjects (baptism, the Eucharist, free will, martyrdom, resurrection…) answered with quoted passages from the Fathers, earliest first.
- [Scripture index](https://viapatrum.org/scripture/): Where the Fathers comment on or quote each book and chapter of the Bible.
- [Listen](https://viapatrum.org/listen/): The audio library — works read aloud with sentence-by-sentence read-along highlighting.
- [How we translate](https://viapatrum.org/methodology/): Sources, translation method, and how each text is checked against the Greek or Latin. Read this before characterising the translations.
- [About](https://viapatrum.org/about/): What Via Patrum is and who makes it.

## Structure and citation

- A work lives at `https://viapatrum.org/works/{slug}/` and contains its full text on one page, with stable section anchors: `https://viapatrum.org/works/{slug}/#s5` is section 5.
- Each chapter also has its own page: `https://viapatrum.org/works/{slug}/{n}/` — the best citation target for a specific chapter.
- Short quoted passages on a topic live at `https://viapatrum.org/e/{id}/` ("excerpt" pages). Each names its author, work, chapter, and source edition, and is the best citation target for a single quotation.
- An author's page `https://viapatrum.org/authors/{slug}/` collects their works and their passages by question.
- The complete URL inventory is in the sitemap index: https://viapatrum.org/sitemap.xml (works, chapters, authors, topics, Scripture, excerpts).

## Key works

- [The Letters of Ignatius — Ignatius of Antioch](https://viapatrum.org/works/ignatius-letters/)
- [The Epistle to Diognetus — Anonymous](https://viapatrum.org/works/diognetus-epistle/)
- [Polycarp to the Philippians — Polycarp of Smyrna](https://viapatrum.org/works/polycarp-philippians/)
- [The Martyrdom of Polycarp — Church of Smyrna](https://viapatrum.org/works/martyrdom-polycarp/)
- [On Prayer — Origen of Alexandria](https://viapatrum.org/works/origen-on-prayer/)
- [On the Resurrection of the Dead — Athenagoras](https://viapatrum.org/works/athenagoras-resurrection/)
- [Who Is the Rich Man That Shall Be Saved? — Clement of Alexandria](https://viapatrum.org/works/clement-alexandria-rich-man/)

The full list of all 328 works and 78 authors is in [llms-full.txt](https://viapatrum.org/llms-full.txt).

## Rights and reuse

- Reading on the site is free, and streaming read-along audio is free.
- The underlying ancient texts are public domain. English translations are Via Patrum's own, made from the Greek and Latin and checked against them, except where a page credits a public-domain source translation (e.g. Ante-Nicene Fathers) — the credit line on each work and excerpt page governs that text.
- Downloads (EPUB, PDF, Word, audiobook files) are provided through a paid library pass; the text itself remains free to read here.
- When quoting, attribute "Via Patrum (viapatrum.org)" and link the work, chapter, or excerpt page.
